heroHeadline: Brugada Launches 'Código 1' Proximity Policing as August Posts Fewest CDMX Homicides in 29 Years, Even as Unión Tepito's Turf War Claims Three More Lives
heroSubtitle: Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada launched the 'Código 1, la policía en tu calle' strategy on September 9 — 2,044 patrol units and 8,176 officers walking 1,022 redrawn cuadrantes, backed by 3,500 new patrol vehicles and a camera network expanded to 120,000 units — while announcing August 2026 closed as the capital's lowest-homicide August in 29 years. She also unveiled a Ley de Justicia Cívica reform (Sept 5) to expand civic courts and community mediation. Even so, the Unión Tepito vs. Anti-Unión turf war in the Centro Histórico claimed three more lives in a single week: alleged Unión Tepito member 'El Chilaquil' was shot dead in Peralvillo on September 4, and two days later rival figure 'El Tripa' and his wife were gunned down leaving Chilaquil's wake in San Rafael — SSC arrested two suspected Unión Tepito gunmen on September 8, in the same week authorities reported roughly 50 combined arrests across both factions during August.
footerNote: Data sourced from official CDMX government reports (Gobierno CDMX, SSC, SACMEX, SEMOVI, CAMe, CONAGUA, FGJ-CDMX, Congreso CDMX), INEGI, Fiscalía CDMX, NASA, La Jornada, El Universal, Proceso, Milenio, Infobae México, N+, El Financiero, El Sol de México, Excélsior, La Crónica de Hoy, La Razón, La Silla Rota, El Heraldo de México, Reuters, AP, Euronews, US News, and institutional analyses from UNAM, IMCO, México Evalúa, and the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP).
